note: The reported myocardial damage was based on elevated CK and CK-MB with completely normal cardiac anatomy and function on echocardiogram, a classic presentation of false-positive biomarker elevation in myopathies.

evidence.text: A 19-month-old boy with LGMDR29 was diagnosed with myocardial injury based on elevated CK and CK-MB following influenza A, despite normal cardiac structure and systolic function on echocardiography.

source.title: A Case of Limb-Girdle Muscular Dystrophy Type R29 Presenting with Myocardial Damage as the Initial Manifestation: A case report
source.quote: Cardiac structure and function, as assessed by echocardiography, were found to be normal, and the patient did not exhibit any typical symptoms of muscle weakness.

evidence.text: Patients with skeletal myopathies frequently display false-positive cardiac biomarker elevations due to cross-reactivity and expression of cardiac markers in regenerating skeletal muscle.

source.title: False-Positive Causes in Serum Cardiac Troponin Levels
source.quote: A number of studies have reported elevated serum cTn levels in many patients with skeletal myopathies even in the absence of ischemia and... cross-reactions of diagnostic (anti-cTn) antibodies with skeletal troponins.
